newsitem.title: USA: Earthgrains Q1 net up on cost-cutting.
newsitem.headline: Earthgrains Q1 net up on cost-cutting.

text.p: Earthgrains Co, which makes fresh baked goods and refrigerated dough, said Monday its first quarter income was up sharply due in part to lower manufacturing costs and improved operating efficiencies.
Earthgrains reported earnings for the first quarter ended June 17 of $0.68 a share, up from $0.07 a year ago.

Revenues of $377.4 million were up 1.9 percent from last year's $370.5 million despite the unfavorable impact of foreign exchange rates. Without the exchange rate impact, revenues would have increased 4.7 percent.
Contributing to sales growth for the largest business, U.S. bakery products, were improved volume and brand mix, increased prices and last year's acquisition of Heiner's Bakery of Huntington, W.Va.
"Our first-quarter results reflect another positive step in our turnaround progress and the effectiveness of our business strategies," Chairman Barry Beracha said in a statement.

The quarterly operating margin was 3.5 percent, up from 0.8 percent a year ago. "We continue to show progress toward our goals for improved profitability, including an operating margin of five percent by fiscal 2000," Beracha said.
